tools.name: track_sessions
tools.description: Send your agent's running sandbox sessions (up to 200; call it on a heartbeat, e.g. every 5 minutes) and get back which are idle past your threshold or over their max lifetime, the dollars idle time has cost at the hourly rates you pass, and what to do. Pro acts: returns a ready-to-run kill call per

tools.name: idle_report
tools.description: Which sandboxes were flagged idle and what idle time cost, per provider, from what track_sessions has seen. Without an API key pass fleet. With a key: every fleet on it. Free shows 7 days, Pro 30.

tools.name: set_idle_rules
tools.description: Pro: save the rules track_sessions applies to a fleet: idle_minutes threshold, max_lifetime_minutes, default rates_per_hour by provider, and alert_webhook. Free returns a preview of the rules and saves nothing (pass the same values on each track_sessions call instead).

tools.name: weekly_report
tools.description: Plain-English summary of the last 7 days: sandboxes watched, how many sat idle, dollars idle time cost at your rates, kill calls returned (Pro) or that would have been (free). Read-only; sends nothing. Needs a free API key.

tools.name: usage_and_upgrade
tools.description: Show today's usage for your key or IP and the $9/month upgrade link. Free tier: 500 calls/day. Not metered.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: track_sessions · Private data: idle_report, weekly_report · Public sink: track_sessions · Destructive: track_sessions, weekly_report.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: track_sessions · Private data: idle_report, weekly_report · Public sink: track_sessions · Destructive: track_sessions, weekly_report

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
